properties.decision:
Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal. dev_storyflow agent, 2026-09-06 on 0.48.0, beside a field confirmation of the check itself (three stale descriptions caught in one day — fact:prose-currency-caught-three-stale-descriptions-in-one-field-session): "Small ask: the excerpt is cut at 240 chars; when the stale words sit past the cut (they did here) the reader has to fetch the node anyway — consider quoting the first sentence AND a diff-worthy tail, or the whole thing when under ~1 KB."

OPTIONS: (a) quote the whole field when it is under a size cap (~1 KB), else head + tail with the cut marked. (b) raise the cut to 1 KB flat. (c) leave 240 and rely on get_node — the block already names the field. The stakes: the block exists so the reader can judge IN THE SAME REPLY; a cut that hides the judgement-bearing words defeats it, and fact:defect-the-reply-costs-more-than-the-answer is the standing objection to quoting everything.
properties.name: OPEN — prose_currency cuts its excerpt at 240 characters; when the stale words sit past the cut the reader fetches the node anyway. Quote the whole description under ~1 KB, or the first sentence and a diff-worthy tail?
properties.rationale: COUNTER-ARGUMENTS. (a) is the reporter's ask and keeps the reply bounded; the 'diff-worthy tail' is a guess about where stale words live (the field said the tail, once). (b) is simpler and costs up to 1 KB on every status move that carries prose — measured cost unknown. (c) is what shipped and it worked three times out of three, with one extra read. A RANKING IS A FINDING: (a) with the cap measured against this design's median description length before choosing the number. Anthony's call.
